- scripts/unblock_actions.py:352-363 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: For a project-child security issue (ctx["kind"] == "issue", ctx["tracking"] set, _is_security_issue(ctx) returns True, ctx.get("security_finding_id") truthy), the plan() function still emits create_issue and close operations before the comment.
  WHY: The reissue verdict for a project-child ai:security issue should not create a standalone replacement or close the original. The linked issue (AD-2) says to keep the original open when it belongs to a project. The current code unconditionally appends create_issue in the else branch (kind="issue", line 358), unconditionally appends close when security_finding_id is truthy (line 360), and only then appends the stays-open comment (line 363).
- Requirement: "On reissue, preserve the security label and finding marker on the replacement; if that cannot be done safely, keep the original open." (issue #6274, AD-2: "Either keep the original open, or copy the ai:security label and the finding marker onto the replacement issue")
  Expected change site: scripts/unblock_actions.py::plan reissue branch — the else-branch (kind="issue") should skip create_issue and close when security_issue and ctx["tracking"] are both truthy, and should instead post a comment on the tracking issue requesting a re-issue.
  Evidence of absence: The LAST RUN DIFF only modifies the comment body text (lines 359-362 of scripts/unblock_actions.py). The else-branch still unconditionally appends create_issue (line 358), still appends close whenever ctx.get("security_finding_id") is truthy (line 360), and the trailing stays-open comment block still posts on item (the original) rather than also posting a comment on ctx["tracking"] to complete the two-comment shape. The test test_security_reissue_keeps_a_finding_open_or_transfers_its_marker asserts exactly ["comment", "comment"] with the first comment on issue 12 (tracking) and the second on issue 7 (original), which no current code path produces.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
